newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk hopeful on generator pacts.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk hopeful on generator pacts.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp said it remained hopeful that it would reach an agreement with independent power producers by year end.

About a year after Niagara Mohawk unveiled PowerChoice -- its vision for a competitive electricity market -- the company said contracts with unregulated generators remain a roadblock to implementing that proposal.
The utility buys power from the generators under contracts mandated under state and federal regulations.

PowerChoice, announced in October 1995, was cited by New York regulators as a model for the restructuring proposals sought from other electric utilities, were ordered to file the plans with the State Public Service Commission by October 1.
In August, Niagara Mohawk said, it offered to buy out 44 unregulated generator contracts that represent 90 percent of its above-market power costs, which currently total about $66 million a month.

Under the offer, the unregulated generators would be compensated with a combination of cash and securities from a restructured Niagara Mohawk, it said. Discussions on the offer are continuing, it said.

"While we wanted to achieve a negotiated solution with the unregulated generators before now, we remain hopeful that an agreement will be reached by the end of the year," said William E. Davis, Niagara Mohawk's chief executive.
"In addition to clearing the way for PowerChoice, a solution to the unregulated generator problem also will eliminate the need for our pending rate increase request," he said.
